config.objective: Win + 0.5 draw; ties broken by normalized remaining team HP difference, then target damage, then canonical item key.
config.scope: All 220 unordered three-finished-item multisets, including repeated items. No component availability constraint. Canonical inventory order only.

items.name: Focus Sash
items.short: Survives a lethal hit with 1 HP: becomes untargetable and inactive for 1.5s (enemies drop it as a target), is cleansed of damage-over-time effects, and returns with a shield worth 10% of its HP (once)

items.name: Leftovers
items.short: Restores 1% of its HP per second

items.name: Life Orb
items.short: +24% to all its damage; loses 2% HP per basic attack

items.name: Quick Claw
items.short: Starts combat with 20% Energy and recovers 8% every time it uses its ability

items.name: Rocky Helmet
items.short: Returns 18% of the basic-attack damage it takes

items.name: Scope Lens
items.short: +25% Crit chance on basic attacks; its crits deal ×1.9

items.name: Shell Bell
items.short: Drain: heals 15% of the damage it deals

notes: All calculations are native, synchronous, rendering-free 6v6 battles. No full games or RL training are measured.
All combatants use the target star level; no weather, boons, boss bonuses, or additional shiny boost.
The target gets the searched three items, its five allies one heuristic item each, and opponents eight items across six units.
Mirrored side assignments share each numeric combat seed. Units retain native traits, item effects, AI targeting and combat RNG.
Candidate order can cause diverging RNG consumption; pairing shares starting seeds, not identical random events.
Refinement sees additional training compositions and disjoint seeds. Validation has eight unseen enemy lineups and disjoint seeds.
Best observed is selected among five refinement finalists plus the native heuristic baseline, not among all 220 on validation.

The build selected before validation is also recorded to expose selection changes. Intervals are descriptive, unadjusted paired normal intervals over context/seed blocks with both side assignments grouped.
Results are conditional on these synthetic lineups, gearing and placements. They do not establish global BIS or optimize component allocation/economy.
